images.filename: Charleston (Sullivan’s Island) Lighthouse, Sullivan’s Island, SC (50622801402).jpg
images.caption: Built in 1962, this was the last onshore manned lighthouse built for the explicit purpose of being a navigational aid in the United States.  The interior of the triangular utilitarian steel and aluminum structure has air conditioning and an elevator, with the beacon being the second-most powerful in the Western Hemisphere as far as luminosity, but is not used at its full brightness.  It is a non-contributing resource in the U.S. Coast Guard Historic District, now part of Fort Sumter and Fort Moultrie National Historic Park.
images.alt: Built in 1962, this was the last onshore manned lighthouse built for the explicit purpose of being a navigational aid in the United States. images.filename: Bunker and Charleston Lighthouse, U.S. Coast Guard Station, U.S. Coast Guard Historic District, Sullivan’s Island, SC (50621958278).jpg
images.caption: Originally built in 1891, the old Coast Guard Station has several buildings dating to 1891, 1898, and 1938, which were built during its period of operation as an active United States Coast Guard Station.  Since closed, the station has been repurposed by the National Park Service for their operations at Fort Sumter and Fort Moultrie National Historic Park.
